title: Sunny and the Secret Garden | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka pushes through a dense curtain of wattle branches and finds a hidden garden clearing no bigger than a room — soft grass, moonlight, the smell of night flowers — and sits at the centre of the most private, perfect place. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The branches gave way.

Sunny had been pushing through a dense curtain of wattle for several steps — the narrow kind that grows low and thick, all flowers and branches — and then, suddenly, she was through.

A clearing.

Small. Barely bigger than a room. Perfectly round, as if someone had planned it — though of course no one had. Just the way the wattles had grown. Inside: soft grass, undisturbed. No tracks, no signs that anyone had been here before. Moonlight fell through a gap in the canopy above, straight down, like a light left on.

She stood very still at the entrance.

The garden smelled of night flowers — something sweet and close, a warmth in the air that wasn't temperature. She breathed it in.

She walked slowly to the centre.

The wattle walls surrounded her on all sides. The moonlight column fell over her. The grass under her paws was thick and soft.

She thought: this is mine for tonight.

Not mine to keep — the bush doesn't work that way. But mine for right now.

She turned slowly in the centre, looking at the walls of wattle, the moonlit column, the perfect grass.

She sat down.

The secret garden held her.

Close, sweet, perfectly her size.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, secret garden. Goodnight, little one.
